---
title: "quarto-index self-reference probe"
from: markdown-smart
filters:
  - index
---

# A cross-reference that points at its own entry

"Cats, see Cats" tells a reader nothing and, in HTML, links an entry to itself.
Such a target is reported and dropped; the term is then indexed as usual, which
is the one outcome that neither leaves useless output nor loses the term.

Four shapes, so that no single one stands in for the family:

A single-level `see=` naming its own `entry=`: [cats]{.index entry="Cats"
see="Cats"}.

A `see-also=` naming its own two-level `entry=` path: [owls]{.index
entry="Birds!Owls" see-also="Birds!Owls"}.

A self-target on a mark whose entry comes from its visible text rather than
from `entry=`: [ferrets]{.index see="ferrets"}.

A mark carrying both attributes, of which only the `see=` is self-targeting —
the surviving `see-also=` must still be emitted, and the both-attributes report
must still fire: [dogs]{.index entry="Dogs" see="Dogs" see-also="Pets"}.

# A cross-reference that does not

A target naming a different entry is untouched, and is what tells a
self-reference check from a check that drops every target:
[lynxes]{.index entry="Lynxes" see="Cats"}.

# A self-reference the comparison could not see

Two shapes hide a self-reference from a comparison run on the author's
unclamped levels. Both are the same rule M08 states — a self-target is judged
on what the entry PRINTS — applied where printing is not what the author wrote.

The LaTeX back-end stores three levels and folds the rest into the third, so a
deeper entry prints a path the author never spelled. A target spelling that
folded path is a self-reference in LaTeX and is not one in HTML, which has no
ceiling. Three shapes, so that neither the depth nor the attribute nor the
presence of a sort key stands in for the family:

Depth four, `see-also=`: [alpha]{.index entry="A!B!C!D" see-also="A!B!C, D"}.

Depth five, `see=`, where the printed third level joins two folded levels:
[foxtrot]{.index entry="F!G!H!I!J" see="F!G!H, I, J"}.

A folded entry carrying a sort key, where the path it FILES under and the path
it PRINTS are different strings and only the printed one is a self-reference:
[mike]{.index entry="M!N!O!P" sort="m!n!o!p" see-also="M!N!O, P"}.

An empty level prints nothing, so an entry whose non-empty levels are the
target's does read "X, see X" — but the two spellings differ, because a target
drops its empty levels and an entry keeps them. This is format-neutral: it is
true wherever the mark is rendered, so both back-ends report it, and so does a
format with no index back-end at all.

Two levels, the second empty, so the fold cannot reach it and the empty-level
path is what is being tested: [moles]{.index entry="Moles!" see="Moles"}.

Four levels, the last empty — the fold and the empty level at once:
[papa]{.index entry="P!Q!R!" see-also="P!Q!R"}.
